candidate.answerReason: Noon to midnight uses 720 minutes, leaving 280 minutes, or 4 hours 40 minutes. The ending time is 4:40 a.m. the next day, matching choice D.

methods.label: Count through midnight
methods.explanation:
Use midnight as a stopping point, since it is \(12\) hours after noon. With \(60\) minutes in an hour, reaching midnight uses
\[
12\times60=720\text{ minutes}.
\]
The time remaining after midnight is
\[
1000-720=280\text{ minutes}.
\]
Since \(280=4\times60+40\), the contest continues for another \(4\) hours and \(40\) minutes after midnight. It therefore ends at \(\boxed{4\!:\!40\text{ a.m.}}\) the next day, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary hour-minute conversion, subtraction, and counting forward from midnight, all within AMC 8 scope.

candidate.annotationRationale: Hour-minute conversion is an assessed target covered by cnm_p062. In the written method, cnm_p063 supports only finding the local interval from noon to midnight; its stated scope does not cover finding an ending time from a duration. The part-total relationship in cnm_p035 supports subtracting the minutes already used. The ending-time target is proposed separately because the supplied catalog lacks that procedure.
